problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
(x+1)\frac{dy}{dx}=2{y}^{1/2}(x+1)^{3}+2y,\,y(0)=\frac{1}{4},\,x>-1.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{x+1}\,z=(x+1)^{2}
$$

using the substitution $z={y}^{1/2}.$*
worked_solution:
The substitution $z={y}^{1/2}$ transforms the given equation into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{x+1}\,z=(x+1)^{2},
$$

with the initial condition

$$
z(0)=\sqrt{y(0)}=\frac{1}{2}\,.
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)
$$

with

$$
P(x)=-\frac{1}{x+1},\,Q(x)=(x+1)^{2}\,.
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{-\int 1/(x+1)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)^{-1}} \\  & =(x+1)^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

under the condition that $x>-1.$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)=(x+1)^{-1}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x+1}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{x+1}\,z) & =\frac{1}{x+1}\cdot (x+1)^{2} \\ \frac{1}{x+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\,z & =x+1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x+1}\,z) & =x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x+1}\,z)\,\text{d}x & =\int (x+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{x+1}\,z & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x+C \\ z & =(x+1)(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x+C)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we determine the value of $C$ that satisfies the initial condition $z(0)=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z(0) & =\frac{1}{2} \\ (0+1)(\frac{1}{2}{0}^{2}+0+C) & =\frac{1}{2} \\ C & =\frac{1}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have 

$$
z=(x+1)(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x+\frac{1}{2})\,.
$$

Finally, we determine $y(x)$ by substituting the solution into $z={y}^{1/2}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{1/2} & =(x+1)(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x+\frac{1}{2}) \\ y & =(x+1)^{2}{(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
